description.summary: A rare atmospheric electrical phenomenon appearing as luminous, spherical objects that float through air during thunderstorms. Scientifically confirmed but not fully understood.
description.full: Ball lightning is an unexplained atmospheric electrical phenomenon described as luminous, spherical objects that vary from pea-sized to several meters in diameter. Typically appearing during thunderstorms, these glowing orbs have been reported to float or move erratically through the air, pass through solid objects, and last from seconds to minutes before disappearing—sometimes silently, sometimes with an explosion. Despite centuries of eyewitness reports and recent photographic evidence, the physical mechanism behind ball lightning remains poorly understood. Various theories involve plasma physics, silicon vaporization, microwave cavities, and chemical reactions, but no single explanation fully accounts for all reported characteristics. The phenomenon is real but represents one of nature's most enigmatic displays.

behavior.movement_pattern: Floats horizontally at roughly human height, may follow air currents or walls

range.description: Worldwide phenomenon, reported wherever thunderstorms occur

origins.cultural_roots: Reported across all cultures with thunderstorm activity
origins.earliest_accounts: Ancient Greek and Roman texts mention fiery spheres during storms
origins.scientific_skepticism: Long dismissed as optical illusion, retinal afterimage, or hallucination

history.modern_era: Ball lightning is now accepted as real but remains poorly understood. Research focuses on laboratory recreation and theoretical models.

notable.name: Lanzhou Spectroscopic Observation
notable.description: Chinese researchers studying regular lightning accidentally captured ball lightning on video and spectrometer. The white, spherical object appeared after lightning strike, lasted 1.64 seconds, and moved horizontally. Spectroscopic analysis revealed silicon, iron, and calcium, supporting silicon vaporization theory.

credibility.notes: First and only spectroscopic analysis of ball lightning to date

sources: Cen, J., et al. (2014). Physical Review Letters, 112(3)

notable.name: Great Thunderstorm of Widecombe
notable.description: During church service, ball lightning entered church during thunderstorm, killed four people, injured 60. Multiple witnesses described glowing sphere moving through church. One of best-documented historical cases.

credibility.notes: Multiple witnesses, contemporary documentation, physical damage recorded
